subject: Urquhart et al. (2016)
object: Urquhart et al. (2016) reported a consanguineous family with 3 affected sibs who had a severe prenatal neurodevelopmental disorder. Features included fronto-parietal pachygyria, agenesis of the corpus callosum, and progressive severe microcephaly.

subject: Urquhart et al. (2016)
object: In the 3 affected sibs of a consanguineous family with CDCBM17, Urquhart et al. (2016) used autozygosity mapping and exome sequencing to identify a novel homozygous 1-bp deletion in the DMRTA2 gene (c.1197delT). The deletion was predicted to cause a frameshift (p.Pro400LeufsTer33). The authors stated that data from murine and zebrafish knockout models were consistent with the variant being responsible for the cortical phenotype. They suggested that loss of function of DMRTA2 leads to a novel disorder of cortical development.
